data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemeni forces say strikes conducted against Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Yemeni forces say strikes conducted against Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada
Yemen's armed forces said early on Sunday it was conducting strikes against the Houthis in the capital Sanaa and the group's stronghold Saada.
A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, which are aligned with the internationally recognised government, said forces were targeting what he described as "vital targets", without providing further details.
Yemen's Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported earlier an attack it said was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Sanaa. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation on the report.
The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and forces aligned with the Saudi-backed government mostly stopped after a 2022 truce, but fighting has broken out again in a spillover from the wider war between Iran and the United States.
Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
Saudi Arabia has responded with air strikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to repel the Houthis.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Hegseth: US blockade of Hormuz ironclad, Iran should make right choice
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Hegseth: US blockade of Hormuz ironclad, Iran should make right choice
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said that the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is “ironclad” and that US President Donald Trump has “all the options he needs on the table” if Iran continues to “play games” with the strait, according to an AP report carried by the Times of Israel.
“Iran wants to play games with things like the Strait of Hormuz. They don’t control it, we do,” Hegseth told reporters.
“They have literally gotten nothing through. Our blockade has been ironclad and we’re running almost at prewar levels every single night through that, you see that as far as the throughput.”
He added: “So we feel like we’re in a very strong position. Iran ought make the right choice. If they don’t, the president is going to have all the options he needs on the table. But he is not going to let these things extend unnecessarily. He understands what the mission is and we can get it done when called upon.”
Hegseth also said that Trump is “hellbent” on Iran not having a nuclear weapon, the report said.
“The message is very simple: Iran will never ever ever have a nuclear weapon. President Trump is hell-bent and determined to ensure that they do not; they will not,” Hegseth said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands
Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned the United Arab Emirates (UAE) against challenging Tehran and its sovereignty over three islands in the Persian Gulf.
In a post on his X account, Velayati dismissed recent claims made by the UAE at the United Nations General Assembly regarding sovereignty over Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb, and Abu Musa, saying the three islands will remain Iranian forever, according to IRNA.
"A country whose political life does not reach half a century makes claims from the UN podium about islands that have been recorded under Iran's name in historical documents and maps of past centuries," Velayati said in the Farsi-language post.
He added that the UAE should not "rely on foreign powers" for its security and should instead pursue good relations with its neighbours, IRNA reported.
"The neighbour stays, and the guest goes… Regional experience has shown that imported security has an expiration date," said the former Iranian foreign minister.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says
Attacks on commercial ships witnessed a surge during the past three days, as at least three tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz, according to United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) warnings.
Early Saturday, UKMTO reported that a crude oil tanker was hit on its port side approximately 4 nautical miles east of Oman.
A day earlier, an outbound vessel suffered a small fire and blackout, while a second crude tanker was struck nearby.
On Thursday, a supertanker carrying 2.5 million barrels caught fire after being hit off Oman while transiting an unauthorised route, according to Iran's Fars news agency.
In its weekly Voluntary Reporting Area Overview released on 2 October, UKMTO said 91 incidents of damage to vessels have been reported since February this year.
Three tankers have been struck in and around the Strait of Hormuz since 1 October 2026. (AFP)

'See what was done to Gaza': Angelina Jolie shares images of destruction
American actress Angelina Jolie has posted before-and-after Google Maps satellite images showing the scale of destruction across Gaza.
"You can now open Google Earth and see what was done to Gaza," Jolie wrote in a long post on X.
"Whole neighbourhoods have been reduced to rubble. Homes, schools, universities, hospitals, roads, water and sanitation systems, infrastructure that people depended on to survive have been damaged or destroyed,” she wrote.
She said some 1.98 million people in Gaza need humanitarian assistance, but noted that “aid and shelter materials continue to face restrictions and delays”.

data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iran arrests 31 people linked to 'US-Israel sabotage networks', report says
At least 31 people linked to four networks backed by the US and Israel have been arrested in Iran on charges of fomenting unrest and carrying out acts of sabotage, Iran's Press TV reported.
Iran's Intelligence Ministry, which made the arrests in southern Kerman province, said the suspects in Sirjan county were organised into networks to “lure teenagers and young people” and had prepared “large quantities of Molotov cocktails” to “damage urban surveillance cameras in preparation for street unrest and acts of sabotage”.
The ministry also accused the groups of “violence and destruction” during the January nationwide protests.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran opens military centre for citizens, 'training 1,000 battalions'
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iran opens military centre for citizens, 'training 1,000 battalions'
Iran opened a military training centre in Tehran on Saturday, which is said to be aimed at preparing citizens to confront US and Israeli forces in the event of a ground attack.
US-Israeli attacks on 28 February triggered seven months of conflict. A truce on 8 April halted 40 days of war, but sporadic hostilities continued.
The new centre at Haft-e Tir Square followed a first camp at Imam Hussein Square, hoping to train civilians in the coming weeks.
Footage from the centre showed army members conducting drills with camouflage-painted anti-aircraft equipment, crossing obstacle courses and using virtual reality headsets to train with weapons.
At a news conference, Ali Kowsari, deputy for training at the Basij organisation, said 1,000 battalions had been prepared for training. Kowsari stressed the importance of civil defence across society.
He said Iranians would stand united against any new attack if the enemy made "another miscalculation".
An Iranian officer demonstrates the use of a man-portable air-defense system during the inauguration of a training centre for volunteers at Haft-e-Tir Square in Tehran on 3 October 2026. (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli forces, settlers continue campaign of detentions and attacks in West Bank
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli forces, settlers continue campaign of detentions and attacks in West Bank
Several Palestinians were detained by Israeli forces, while settlers continued attacks on Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank since Saturday evening, according to reports.
* Israeli forces detained three Palestinian farmers and seized a truck loaded with bananas in the Ras al-Ahmar area, southeast of Tubas, according to Mutaz Basharat, the Tubas governorate official in charge of the Jordan Valley file, Wafa reported.
*Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli soldiers, attacked Palestinian homes on Saturday evening in the Wadi al-Hasin and Harat Jaber areas of Hebron’s Old City, south of the occupied West Bank. The assailants shouted threats and insults and used obscene language, Wafa reported. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition toward Palestinian homes in the area.
*Israeli settlers attacked and wounded a 27-year-old Palestinian man in the village of Usarin, south of Nablus. Medical sources told Wafa that the injured man was transferred to a hospital for treatment.
*Israeli forces launched an arrest campaign in the village of Burqa, in the Nablus district, north of the West Bank, Al Jazeera reported.
*Israeli forces raided the homes of Palestinian residents of the town of Kafr Qaddum, east of Qalqilya, while settlers attacked a home near Najah Hospital, north of Nablus city, according to Al Jazeera.
*Clashes erupted between Palestinians and Israeli forces during a raid on Deir Jarir village, east of Ramallah.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel says 1, 318 personnel killed since 7 Oct Hamas attack
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israel says 1, 318 personnel killed since 7 Oct Hamas attack
Israeli defence ministry has said that a total of 1,318 Israeli personnel have been killed since Hamas’s 7 October 2023 attack.
The figures include all soldiers, police officers, Shin Bet agents, firefighters, prison warders, and civilian officers who died on and since 7 October 2023, whether in "the line of duty or as a result of an accident, illness, or suicide", according to the Times of Israel.
Most were killed during fighting in the Gaza Strip, Lebanon, and the West Bank, it added.
The ministry said the conflict has added more than 7,150 family members to Israel’s circle of bereavement, including 2,143 parents, 355 widows, 880 children and 3,772 siblings.

data.title: Middle East Eye: NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations
Israeli embassies in the United States and the United Kingdom are promoting a copycat NAZA, nearly a month after the release of the original that focuses on testimony of Israelis killing Palestinians in Gaza.
In posts on X, the embassies said that "Naza: The Real Story" is "setting the record straight" and claims to offer a firsthand account from senior Israeli military commanders and intelligence officers directly involved in Israel's genocidal war on Gaza.
It said the film uses combat footage, declassified materials, captured intelligence and firsthand testimony to give context on "how the war was fought and the challenges Israeli forces faced".
The film's website names the provider as Three Musketeers Production, "a company in formation", and says a registered address and registration number will be published once the company is registered. It says the directors are deliberately not named "for their safety".
Claimed to have been filmed on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the 49-minute documentary is available in 17 languages on its official website.

data.summary:
Six-year-old killed by Israeli attacks in central Gaza
A six-year-old Palestinian girl has succumbed to wounds sustained in an Israeli attack in central Gaza's Deir el-Balah, Wafa news agency reports, citing medical sources.
According to the sources, Suha Mohammed Nasser was shot by Israeli forces while sheltering with her family in a tent in Wadi al-Salqa, south of Deir al-Balah.
In a separate attack, Saqr al-Qaisi was killed when an Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the city's al-Hawouz area.
Meanwhile, in southern Gaza, Israeli shelling continues to pound Khan Younis's Sheikh Nasser neighbourhood.
Al Jazeera reports that in Gaza City, several people have been wounded in an Israeli drone strike near the Abd al-Rahman School in al-Saftawi in the city's north, while another person was shot in the Tuffah neighbourhood. The Israeli military also conducted demolitions in the city's east.
Israeli military vehicles also opened fire east of al-Qarara, north of Khan Younis, and north of Beit Lahiya.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions
Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until Washington meets certain conditions.
Ghalibaf, who also acts as Tehran's chief negotiator in the talks, said that the contested waterway will remain closed until seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding are met by Washington.
He conceded that the US had made "some proposals through a mediator" after Tehran presented a seven-day roadmap to reopen the strait.
But he warned Washington that "the era of wasting time and dictating unilateral demands is over" and Iran's position remains "clear and definite".

In France, a unique app certifies shopkeepers boycotting products linked to Israeli settlements while promoting alternative brands

Among the many apps available on the Play Store, one stands out thanks to its heart‑shaped icon featuring a Palestinian flag: “Gaza Friendly”.
Created in June 2025, the label certifies shopkeepers involved in the boycott of products originating from the occupied Palestinian territories and marketed by companies supporting Israel’s settlement expansion.
To date, the app and its associated website list 80 businesses in France, mainly butchers, restaurants, bakeries, caterers, tea rooms and food distributors.
The list is updated regularly, and the app features an interactive map allowing consumers to locate certified shops near their homes.
The app, which has been downloaded more than 500 times so far, was created by Pierre-Amael Noailly Charny, a paediatrician of Tunisian origin from Lyon, in east-central France, along with a small group of friends.
Noailly Charny explains that shopkeepers who join Gaza Friendly can express their commitment to the Palestinian cause in a concrete way.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman: Strait of Hormuz 'main concern' of leadership
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman: Strait of Hormuz 'main concern' of leadership
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, has said that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is the "main focus" of truce talks with Washington.
Speaking at a news conference, Baghaei said that Tehran is "focusing on the strait foremost", and that its primary concern is "to reach a solution and to have peace and stability restored within this waterway". He added that, by contrast, Washington's strategy to end the conflict is focused on Iran's nuclear file.
He told reporters that the return of International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors has not been discussed by Iran's leadership.
He noted that the peace process has been thwarted by the "volatility and fluctuation" of Washington's decision-making.
“This is reflected in their conflicting statements as well as their fluctuating demands. This is a problem faced not only by Iran, but by all the countries dealing with the United States. These countries are openly complaining about the crisis,” said Baghaei said.
Meanwhile, Tasnim news agency reports that Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a meeting with foreign ambassadors that there is "no military solution or any solution based on new sanctions" to the seven-month-long conflict.
“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi said.
He added that Tehran is “serious about finding diplomatic solutions, just as we are serious about defending ourselves”.
